- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., < -0.30) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–8% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day mean by 1–3% in early cycles; apply mean reversion bias correction by subtracting 0.5–1.5% from forecast mean.
- When sentiment is neutral (±0.10–0.20), model tends to lag 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by -0.5 to -1.0% to align with true momentum.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative trend, model often fails to capture the reversal; add 1–3% upward bias in next 3–5 days.
